Flight controllers received the spacecraft’s call Thursday, exactly 24 hours after it was sent. That’s how long it took for the radio signal to traverse the more than 26 billion kilometres (16 billion miles) at the speed of light.

stories.title: The secret of 'strange metals' may lie in quantum statistics, not collisions
stories.summary: In an ordinary metal, electrons behave like well-defined particles that occasionally bump into imperfections or vibrations of the crystal. Many materials with strong electron–electron interactions, including the copper-oxide (cuprate) superconductors, break these rules. In these "strange metals," electrical resistance rises in a straight line with temperature over a very wide range. Electrons seem to lose their momentum at the fastest rate quantum mechanics allows, the so-called Planckian limit. What causes this is still an open question.

stories.title: Scientists Discover a Possible Marker in the Blood of C.T.E. Patients
stories.summary: Researchers have found that a blood test used for Alzheimer's can also detect a protein fragment that points to CTE. A simple blood test could identify CTE in living patients — a groundbreaking innovation at a time when the traumatic brain disease can only be diagnosed after someone’s death. “This is a game changer,” said Michael Alosco, co-director of clinical research at the Boston University CTE Center and an author of the new study. Recent research has found that as many as 1 in 4 NFL players develop CTE , sometimes leading to disturbing changes in personality and cognition during life. It can develop into addiction, psychosis and violence, and has been linked to higher risk of ALS .

more.text: Right now, the only way to find out if someone had CTE is after they die: their brain tissue must be extracted and be physically examined to confirm it.
If validated in larger trials, the test could help doctors diagnose the neurodegenerative disease before death

At the close of market on Thursday, Anthropic shares were trading at just over $97 with a nearly $1.3tn total market capitalization, $1.75tn fully diluted. While the final share value was higher than the IPO price of $83, it marked a dip from an early high of $111.50. The firm’s shares initially soared 34% when trading got under way on its US market debut on Thursday, valuing the company at more than $2tn. Nonetheless, Anthropic’s ranked among the biggest stock market flotations in history. The artificial intelligence startup, founded in 2021, became one of the most valuable publicly traded businesses in the world. Continue reading...

stories.title: Cameron Fens wins temporary eligibility after suing the NCAA
stories.summary: An Orange County legal court puts Fens on the basketball court, for now. Today's hearing in front of Judge Alyson Grine sought a Temporary Restraining Order (TRO), a legal mechanism now familiar to most college sports fans. A TRO grants one party in a lawsuit temporary relief while a legal argument proceeds in court. The basic idea is that a party suffering harm while the lawsuit unfolds cannot recover that harm even if he or she wins their case. In other words, Fens' lawyers today argued that Fens' suit has enough merit to be successful but that missing games now irreparably harms him. Those games can't be given back if he wins his suit in a few months.
